verdicts.why: Leading a certain kind of life is stated plainly; the style is named by what follows the verb, not judged by the verb.
Continuing to be alive is a plain fact with no attitude in the word.
Approving: chosen over 'exist', this sense endorses the way of life as real living against mere getting by ('you haven't lived until...').
Having firsthand experience of something ('lived through it') describes without taking a side on it.
In the chance sense, fortune names the unpredictable cause neutrally; it can go either way and the word does not favour one.
Leaving something behind unintentionally is a plain statement of what happened, not a verdict on the person.
Uncertainty about something's truth is named plainly; 'there is some question' takes no side.
Coy and jocular: 'the question' for a proposal treats it with an affectionate wink rather than naming it plainly.
A motion before an assembly is a technical parliamentary term with no attitude.
Finding the solution is plain description of an outcome.
Understanding the meaning of something is stated neutrally.
The optical sense of making detail visible is a technical term with no judgement.
The chemical sense of going into solution is technical and attitude-free.
Exercising memory is the plainest possible naming of a mental act.
Commemorating names an honouring act, but the honour lies in the referent, not in an attitude the word adds.
'Remember me to her' is a courtesy formula; the goodwill is its meaning, not an attitude beyond it.
Mentioning favourably in prayer has the favour built into the meaning; the word itself does not judge the person.
Showing appreciation with a gift or bequest is described discreetly but without the word judging its object.
Saying something again is plain report of an act.
Doing something over is plain description with no attitude.
Restating a musical theme is a technical term with no judgement.
The region above the ground is a plain physical referent.
A slight wind's refreshing quality is part of what the word means, not an attitude the speaker adds toward it.
The atmosphere is a plain physical referent.
The broadcasting medium ('on air') is a technical sense with no judgement.
